claims.exact_statement: For q equal to the four-bit Boolean sign with LSB-first +1 mask 56242, F=A(q), Q=F^{tensor 4}, and W=A(Q), the SMR threshold c_W(eta) is affine and satisfies c_W(eta)>c_F(eta) for every eta>=0. At eta=1/4, c_W=2.133840018016030...>2.1338. Hence universal SMR(c,1/4) requires c>2.1338.
hypotheses: fresh fair selectors in both activations
four disjoint copies in the tensor product
claims.first_unproved_line: No universal finite upper bound c for SMR(c,eta) is proved.

claims.exact_statement: For disjoint Boolean products, U,I,G,B,M and L_{c,eta} are additive, so tensor powers alone leave the normalized SMR threshold unchanged.
claims.refutes: unqualified tensor amplification of an SMR threshold
